can_answer: yes: annual recorded counts of motorist and cyclist deaths can be compared directly; this does not measure an individual's or road user's risk of death
metric: Annual number of recorded motorist deaths and cyclist deaths, each calculated as the sum of its corresponding *_killed column
denominator: None; these are counts of recorded people killed, not rates
population: All police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash rows with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; the two death measures include nonmissing values of their respective killed columns
grouping: Calendar year, with two series: motorist deaths and cyclist deaths

data_check.population_rows_by_year: Recorded in check_1.csv; every year 2013–2025 has dates from January 1 through December 31.
data_check.filter_and_group_column: crash_date is a DATE, so empty strings and unknown words cannot occur as values; no rows have NULL dates, and no rows use 1900-01-01 or 1970-01-01 defaults. No impossible date values can be represented by the DATE type.
data_check.outcome_missing_rows: number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed each have zero missing rows in every included year.

missing_data_decisions: Keep all in-range crash rows and count their nonmissing killed-column values; no in-range rows are dropped or outcomes omitted due to missingness. All years are complete calendar years in the file.
plan_adjustment: No change to the initial framing; the check supports retaining all eligible rows and outcomes.
limitations: These are police-reported death counts, not individual risk or exposure-adjusted rates; conclusions are limited to recorded NYC crash deaths.
